Quick legal-style redline proposal (draft text you can paste into MSA / Order Form):

Publicity and Reference:
1. Customer may identify Supplier (Redwood Inference) as a vendor in short-form marketing materials, press mentions, and digital listings, provided Customer: (a) gives Supplier at least five (5) business days' prior written notice of the proposed publication; (b) provides the final text and proposed use of Supplier marks for Supplier's review (limited to trademark and logo use only); and (c) uses Supplier marks in accordance with Supplier's Logo Usage Guidelines. Supplier's review of short-form references shall be limited to trademark/logo compliance and shall be completed within two (2) business days of receipt and shall not be unreasonably withheld.

2. Any case study, customer quote, testimonial, or extended public materials (>200 words or inclusion of attribution by an identifiable individual) that reference Supplier requires Supplier's prior written approval, which may be withheld in its reasonable discretion.

3. Upon Supplier's written request, Customer shall remove Supplier marks and references within thirty (30) days.

4. Prior to any public announcement referencing Supplier, Customer will deposit the final publication assets (PDF, press release text, and related materials) into a mutually accessible shared folder and provide a link to Supplier within the Order Form addendum.

If that looks good I can tidy for signature. We should accept the 5 business day window for short mentions but insist on the 2-day logo-only review and the escrow requirement. That gives Marketing the operational ability to approve quickly and protects us for actual case studies.

—Lauren (contracts)
